model.reasoning_effort: Pro default; no separate numeric effort setting

available_tools_allowlist: ChatGPT built-in Python execution (if exposed in the run)
tools.network_policy: offline after staging; no web search, no external connectors, no external APIs; the only treatment difference is selection/invocation of Particle Physics Research in B

notes: Model label and mode fixed by user: GPT-6 Pro (Astra Pro), Pro default reasoning configuration.

Browser family/version is recorded from the active ChatGPT Web user-agent metadata; OS is Windows, but build, architecture, CPU, GPU, memory, exact ChatGPT client build, and Python version are not exposed and remain null.

The exact Skill source commit is pinned to the installed plugin's source manifest. The plugin installation-manifest SHA-256 is recorded; per-file source SHA-256 values are in the installation manifest.
A and B require fresh independent ChatGPT Web conversations. A must not select or invoke the plugin; B must explicitly select and invoke the installed Particle Physics Research plugin.
No web search, external connectors, external APIs, or additional plugins are permitted in either arm. Stage identical task inputs before the run.
The 30-minute wall-time and 25-tool-call limits apply equally to both arms. Record token counts only if exposed.
Unexposed host/runtime fields remain null by design; no values are inferred.
The protocol and scoring rules are frozen for Round 1. Do not alter them after observing any pilot outputs.
Protocol v1.1 replaces the private LZ T05 inputs with public pinned sources: two axial-vector paper figure panels and the Native AFH Xe-131 response CSV/export provenance bundle.
T05 Part B is a deterministic presentation transformation of the existing native CSV. It does not rerun the unavailable original AFH package or calculate new nuclear responses.
